195	# its merged `display` is in `code` order, not the authored order, so display_order cannot

218	def _hierarchy_from_parents(codes_to_parent: dict, all_codes: list) -> list:
219	    """
220	    Rebuilds a nested `display` tree for a hierarchical coding from its complete
221	    code -> parent_code edges, once every fragment of a coding split across pages has been
222	    merged. Siblings are ordered by code, since the wire format carries no other order for
223	    a coding the server had to slice.
224	    """
225	    children_of = collections.OrderedDict()
226	    for code in all_codes:
227	        children_of.setdefault(codes_to_parent.get(code, ""), []).append(code)
228	
229	    def subtree(parent_code):
230	        return [
231	            {code: subtree(code)} if code in children_of else code
232	            for code in children_of.get(parent_code, [])
233	        ]
234	
235	    return subtree("")

238	def _finalize_split_codings(codings: dict) -> dict:
239	    """
240	    Turns any coding still carrying `codes_to_parent` back into the canonical shape, now
241	    that every fragment of it has been merged: its edges are a complete parent map, so the
242	    tree hare couldn't safely build from a single page can be built here (see
243	    _hierarchy_from_parents), and the coding is no longer distinguishable from a whole one.
244	    """
245	    for coding in codings.values():
246	        if "codes_to_parent" not in coding:
247	            continue
248	        all_codes = list(coding["codes_to_meanings"])
249	        coding["display"] = _hierarchy_from_parents(
250	            coding.pop("codes_to_parent"), all_codes
251	        )
252	        coding.pop(CODING_PAGINATED_KEY, None)
253	    return codings

256	def get_codings(resp: dict, project_context: str, limit: Optional[int] = None) -> dict:
257	    """
258	    Returns all of the dataset's codings as a dict of coding name to coding, following the
259	    server's pagination cursor and reassembling any coding split across pages.
260	
261	    Each coding has the same shape as a descriptor's `model["codings"]` entry. On the wire, a
262	    hierarchical coding the server had to split sends `codes_to_parent` in place of `display`,
263	    since a tree built from a single page could be wrong; once every fragment is in hand the
264	    edges are complete, so this rebuilds `display` from them before returning -- callers never
265	    see `codes_to_parent`.
266	    """
267	    codings = collections.OrderedDict()
268	    payload = {"project_context": project_context}
269	    if limit is not None:
270	        payload["limit"] = limit
271	
272	    for _ in range(MAX_CODINGS_PAGES):
273	        page = viz_meta_codings_page(resp, payload)
274	        for name, coding in page["results"].items():
275	            if name not in codings:
276	                # Deep-copied so a stored coding never aliases the response, and so every
277	                # key -- not just the ones this function knows to merge -- is safe to keep.
278	                codings[name] = copy.deepcopy(coding)
279	                continue
280	
281	            # Seen already, so the server split this coding across pages. `existing` aliases
282	            # the accumulated coding and is merged into in place.
283	            existing = codings[name]
284	            existing[CODING_PAGINATED_KEY] = True
285	            existing["codes_to_meanings"].update(coding.get("codes_to_meanings") or {})
286	            existing["codes_to_concepts"].update(coding.get("codes_to_concepts") or {})
287	            if "codes_to_parent" in coding:
288	                # A tree built from a single page is wrong, since a code's children can fall
289	                # on the next page; parent edges hold however the pages divide.
290	                existing.setdefault("codes_to_parent", {}).update(
291	                    coding["codes_to_parent"] or {}
292	                )
293	                existing.pop("display", None)
294	            elif "display" in coding and "display" in existing:
295	                existing["display"].extend(coding["display"] or [])
296	
297	        if not page.get("next"):
298	            return _finalize_split_codings(codings)
299	        # Echoed back verbatim as `starting`: when a coding has more codes than `limit`,
300	        # `next` carries that coding's real `after_code` so the next page resumes mid-coding
301	        # at the right code, rather than always just advancing to the next coding name.
302	        payload["starting"] = page["next"]
303	
304	    raise DXError(
305	        "Codings pagination did not complete after {} pages".format(MAX_CODINGS_PAGES)
306	    )

156	    def _get_stage_id(self, stage):
157	        '''
158	        :param stage: A stage ID, name, or index (stage index is the number n for the nth stage, starting from 0; can be provided as an int or a string)
159	        :type stage: int or string
160	        :returns: The stage ID (this is a no-op if it was already a stage ID)
161	        :raises: :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if *stage* could not be parsed, resolved to a stage ID, or it could not be found in the workflow
162	        '''
163	        # first, if it is a string, see if it is an integer
164	        if isinstance(stage, basestring):
165	            try:
166	                stage = int(stage)
167	            except:
168	                # we'll try parsing it as a string later
169	                pass
170	
171	        if not isinstance(stage, basestring):
172	            # Try to parse as stage index; ensure that if it's not a
173	            # string that it is an integer at this point.
174	            try:
175	                stage_index = int(stage)
176	            except:
177	                raise DXError('DXWorkflow: the given stage identifier was neither a string stage ID nor an integer index')
178	            if stage_index < 0 or stage_index >= len(self.stages):
179	                raise DXError('DXWorkflow: the workflow contains ' + str(len(self.stages)) + \
180	                              ' stage(s), and the numerical value of the given stage identifier is out of range')
181	            return self.stages[stage_index].get("id")
182	
183	        if re.compile('^([a-zA-Z_]|stage-)[0-9a-zA-Z_]*$').match(stage) is not None:
184	            # Check if there exists a stage with this stage id
185	            stage_id_exists = any([stg['id'] for stg in self.stages if stg.get('id') == stage])
186	            if stage_id_exists:
187	                return stage
188	
189	        # A stage with the provided ID can't be found in the workflow, so look for it as a name
190	        stage_ids_matching_name = [stg['id'] for stg in self.stages if stg.get('name') == stage]
191	        if len(stage_ids_matching_name) == 0:
192	            raise DXError('DXWorkflow: the given stage identifier ' + stage + ' could not be found as a stage ID nor as a stage name')
193	        elif len(stage_ids_matching_name) > 1:
194	            raise DXError('DXWorkflow: more than one workflow stage was found to have the name "' + stage + '"')
195	        else:
196	            return stage_ids_matching_name[0]

434	            try:
435	                dxpy.api.workflow_update(self._dxid, update_input, **kwargs)
436	            finally:
437	                self.describe() # update cached describe
438	
439	    def is_locked(self):
440	        return self._desc.get('inputs') is not None and self._desc.get('state') == 'closed'
441	
442	    def _get_input_name(self, input_str, region=None, describe_output=None):
443	        '''
444	        :param input_str: A string of one of the forms: "<exported input field name>", "<explicit workflow input field name>", "<stage ID>.<input field name>", "<stage index>.<input field name>", "<stage name>.<input field name>"
445	        :type input_str: string
446	        :returns: If the given form was one of those which uses the stage index or stage name, it is translated to the stage ID for use in the API call (stage name takes precedence)
447	        '''
448	        if '.' in input_str:
449	            stage_identifier, input_name = input_str.split('.', 1)
450	            # Try to parse as a stage ID or name
451	            return self._get_stage_id(stage_identifier) + '.' + input_name
452	
453	        return input_str
454	
455	    def _get_effective_input(self, workflow_input):
456	        effective_input = {}
457	        for key in workflow_input:
458	            input_name = self._get_input_name(key)
459	            if input_name in effective_input:
460	                raise DXError('DXWorkflow: the input for ' + input_name + ' was provided more than once')
461	            effective_input[input_name] = workflow_input[key]
462	        return effective_input
463	
464	    def _get_run_input(self, workflow_input, **kwargs):
465	        effective_workflow_input = self._get_effective_input(workflow_input)
466	
467	        run_input = DXExecutable._get_run_input_common_fields(effective_workflow_input, **kwargs)
468	
469	        if kwargs.get('stage_instance_types') is not None:
470	            run_input['stageSystemRequirements'] = {}
471	            for stage, value in kwargs['stage_instance_types'].items():
472	                if stage != '*':
473	                    stage = self._get_stage_id(stage)
474	                run_input['stageSystemRequirements'][stage] = SystemRequirementsDict.from_instance_type(value).as_dict()
475	
476	        if kwargs.get('stage_folders') is not None:
477	            run_input['stageFolders'] = {}
478	            for stage, value in kwargs['stage_folders'].items():
479	                if stage != '*':
480	                    stage = self._get_stage_id(stage)
481	                run_input['stageFolders'][stage] = value
482	
483	        if kwargs.get('rerun_stages') is not None:
484	            run_input['rerunStages'] = [
485	                _stage if _stage == '*' else self._get_stage_id(_stage)
486	                for _stage in kwargs['rerun_stages']
487	            ]
488	
489	        if kwargs.get('ignore_reuse', False):
490	            run_input['ignoreReuse'] = ['*']
491	
492	        if kwargs.get('ignore_reuse_stages') is not None:
493	            run_input['ignoreReuse'] = [
494	                _stage if _stage == '*' else self._get_stage_id(_stage)
495	                for _stage in kwargs['ignore_reuse_stages']
496	            ]
497	
498	        return run_input
499	
500	    def _run_impl(self, run_input, **kwargs):
501	        return DXAnalysis(dxpy.api.workflow_run(self._dxid, run_input, **kwargs)["id"])
502	
503	    def run(self, workflow_input, *args, **kwargs):
504	        '''
505	        :param workflow_input: Dictionary of the workflow's input arguments; see below for more details
506	        :type workflow_input: dict
507	        :param instance_type: Instance type on which all stages' jobs will be run, or a dict mapping function names to instance types. These may be overridden on a per-stage basis if stage_instance_types is specified.
508	        :type instance_type: string or dict
509	        :param stage_instance_types: A dict mapping stage IDs, names, or indices to either a string (representing an instance type to be used for all functions in that stage), or a dict mapping function names to instance types.
510	        :type stage_instance_types: dict
511	        :param stage_folders: A dict mapping stage IDs, names, indices, and/or the string "*" to folder values to be used for the stages' output folders (use "*" as the default for all unnamed stages)
512	        :type stage_folders: dict
513	        :param rerun_stages: A list of stage IDs, names, indices, and/or the string "*" to indicate which stages should be run even if there are cached executions available
514	        :type rerun_stages: list of strings
515	        :param ignore_reuse_stages: Stages of a workflow (IDs, names, or indices) or "*" for which job reuse should be disabled
516	        :type ignore_reuse_stages: list
517	        :returns: Object handler of the newly created analysis
518	        :rtype: :class:`~dxpy.bindings.dxanalysis.DXAnalysis`
519	
520	        Run the associated workflow. See :meth:`dxpy.bindings.dxapplet.DXExecutable.run` for additional args.
521	
522	        When providing input for the workflow, keys should be of one of the following forms:
523	
524	        * "N.name" where *N* is the stage number, and *name* is the
525	          name of the input, e.g. "0.reads" if the first stage takes
526	          in an input called "reads"
527	
528	        * "stagename.name" where *stagename* is the stage name, and
529	          *name* is the name of the input within the stage
530	
531	        * "stageID.name" where *stageID* is the stage ID, and *name*
532	          is the name of the input within the stage
533	
534	        * "name" where *name* is the name of a workflow level input
535	          (defined in inputs) or the name that has been
536	          exported for the workflow (this name will appear as a key
537	          in the "inputSpec" of this workflow's description if it has
538	          been exported for this purpose)
539	
540	        '''
541	        return super(DXWorkflow, self).run(workflow_input, *args, **kwargs)

32	def verify_string_dxid(dxid, expected_classes):
33	    '''
34	    :param dxid: Value to verify as a DNAnexus ID of class *expected_class*
35	    :param expected_classes: Single string or list of strings of allowed classes of the ID, e.g. "file" or ["project", "container"]
36	    :type expected_classes: string or list of strings
37	    :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if *dxid* is not a string or is not a valid DNAnexus ID of the expected class
38	    '''
39	
40	    if isinstance(expected_classes, basestring):
41	        expected_classes = [expected_classes]
42	    if not isinstance(expected_classes, list) or len(expected_classes) == 0:
43	        raise DXError('verify_string_dxid: expected_classes should be a string or list of strings')
44	    if not (isinstance(dxid, basestring) and
45	            re.match('^(' + '|'.join(expected_classes) + ')-[0-9a-zA-Z]{24}$', dxid)):
46	        if len(expected_classes) == 1:
47	            str_expected_classes = expected_classes[0]
48	        elif len(expected_classes) == 2:
49	            str_expected_classes = ' or '.join(expected_classes)
50	        else:
51	            str_expected_classes = ', '.join(expected_classes[:-1]) + ', or ' + expected_classes[-1]
52	
53	        raise DXError('Invalid ID of class %s: %r' % (str_expected_classes, dxid))

55	class DXObject(object):
56	    """Abstract base class for all remote object handlers."""
57	
58	    def __init__(self, dxid=None, project=None):
59	        # Initialize _dxid and _proj to None values, and have
60	        # subclasses actually perform the setting of the values once
61	        # they have been validated.
62	        self._dxid, self._proj = None, None
63	        self._desc = {}
64	
65	    def _repr(self, use_name=False):
66	        dxid = self._dxid if self._dxid is not None else "no ID stored"
67	        dxproj_id = self._proj if self._proj is not None else "no project ID stored"
68	
69	        if use_name:
70	            if self._class not in ["container", "project", "app", "globalworkflow"]:
71	                desc = "<dxpy.{classname}: {name} ({dxid} ({dxproj_id}))>"
72	            else:
73	                desc = "<dxpy.{classname}: {name} ({dxid})>"
74	        else:
75	            if self._class not in ["container", "project", "app", "globalworkflow"]:
76	                desc = "<{module}.{classname} object at 0x{mem_loc:x}: {dxid} ({dxproj_id})>"
77	            else:
78	                desc = "<{module}.{classname} object at 0x{mem_loc:x}: {dxid}>"
79	
80	        desc = desc.format(module=self.__module__,
81	                           classname=self.__class__.__name__,
82	                           dxid=dxid,
83	                           dxproj_id = dxproj_id,
84	                           mem_loc=id(self),
85	                           name=self._desc.get('name'))
86	        return desc
87	
88	    def __str__(self):
89	        return self._repr(use_name=True)
90	
91	    def __repr__(self):
92	        return self._repr()
93	
94	    def __getattr__(self, attr):
95	        if attr == "__setstate__":
96	            # without this, an infinite recursion occurs when copying an object.
97	            # https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47299243/recursionerror-when-python-copy-deepcopy
98	            raise AttributeError(attr)
99	        if not self._desc:
100	            # describe can fail if the object has not been created
101	            # properly. For example, it has an invalid dxid.
102	            self.describe()
103	        try:
104	            return self._desc[attr]
105	        except:
106	            raise AttributeError()
107	
108	    def describe(self, *args, **kwargs):
109	        '''
110	        Avoid infinite recursion in __getattr__ if describe is not defined.
111	        '''
112	        raise NotImplementedError()
113	
114	    def set_id(self, dxid):
115	        '''
116	        :param dxid: New ID to be associated with the handler
117	        :type dxid: string
118	
119	        Discards the currently stored ID and associates the handler with *dxid*
120	        '''
121	        if dxid is not None:
122	            verify_string_dxid(dxid, self._class)
123	
124	        self._dxid = dxid
125	
126	    def get_id(self):
127	        '''
128	        :returns: ID of the associated object
129	        :rtype: string
130	
131	        Returns the ID that the handler is currently associated with.
132	
133	        '''
134	
135	        return self._dxid

137	class DXDataObject(DXObject):
138	    """Abstract base class for all remote data object handlers.
139	
140	    .. note:: The attribute values below are current as of the last time
141	              :meth:`~dxpy.bindings.DXDataObject.describe` was run.
142	              (Access to any of the below attributes causes
143	              :meth:`~dxpy.bindings.DXDataObject.describe` to be called
144	              if it has never been called before.)
145	
146	    .. py:attribute:: name
147	
148	       String giving the name of the object
149	
150	    .. py:attribute:: folder
151	
152	       String giving the full path to the folder containing the object
153	
154	    .. py:attribute:: types
155	
156	       List of strings indicating the types associated with the object
157	
158	    .. py:attribute:: state
159	
160	       A string containing one of the values "open", "closing", or "closed"
161	
162	    .. py:attribute:: hidden
163	
164	       Boolean indicating whether the object is hidden or not
165	
166	    .. py:attribute:: links
167	
168	       List of strings indicating object IDs that are pointed to by the
169	       object
170	
171	    .. py:attribute:: sponsored
172	
173	       Boolean indicating whether the object is sponsored by DNAnexus
174	
175	    .. py:attribute:: tags
176	
177	       List of strings indicating the tags that are assocated with the
178	       object
179	
180	    .. py:attribute:: created
181	
182	       Timestamp at which the object was created, in milliseconds since
183	       January 1, 1970 at midnight (UTC).
184	
185	    .. py:attribute:: modified
186	
187	       Timestamp at which the object was last modified, in milliseconds
188	       since January 1, 1970 at midnight (UTC).
189	
190	    .. py:attribute:: createdBy
191	
192	       dict containing the following keys and values:
193	
194	       * user: the string ID of the user who created the object or
195	         launched the job that created it
196	       * job (optional): the string ID of the job that created the
197	         object, if a job created the object
198	       * executable (optional): the string ID of the app or applet that
199	         the job was running, if a job created the object
200	
201	    """
202	
203	    def __init__(self, dxid=None, project=None):
204	        if not hasattr(self, '_class'):
205	            raise NotImplementedError(
206	                "DXDataObject is an abstract class; a subclass should be initialized instead.")
207	
208	        DXObject.__init__(self)
209	        self.set_ids(dxid, project)
210	
211	    @staticmethod
212	    def _get_creation_params(kwargs):
213	        common_creation_params = {"project", "name", "tags", "types", "hidden", "properties", "details", "folder", "parents"}
214	
215	        dx_hash = {p: kwargs[p] for p in kwargs if p in common_creation_params and kwargs[p] is not None}
216	        remaining_kwargs = {p: kwargs[p] for p in kwargs if p not in common_creation_params}
217	
218	        if "project" not in dx_hash:
219	            dx_hash["project"] = dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID

221	        return dx_hash, remaining_kwargs

223	    def new(self, **kwargs):
224	        '''
225	        :param project: Project ID in which to create the new remote object
226	        :type project: string
227	        :param name: Name for the object
228	        :type name: string
229	        :param tags: Tags to add for the object
230	        :type tags: list of strings
231	        :param types: Types to add to the object
232	        :type types: list of strings
233	        :param hidden: Whether the object is to be hidden
234	        :type hidden: boolean
235	        :param properties: Properties given as key-value pairs of strings
236	        :type properties: dict
237	        :param details: Details to set for the object
238	        :type details: dict or list
239	        :param folder: Full path to the destination folder
240	        :type folder: string
241	        :param parents: If True, recursively create all parent folders if they are missing
242	        :type parents: boolean
243	
244	        :rtype: :class:`DXDataObject`
245	
246	        Creates a data object with the given fields. Only *project* is
247	        required, and only if no default project or workspace is set;
248	        the remaining arguments are optional and have default behavior
249	        as specified in the API documentation for the ``/new`` method of
250	        each data object class.
251	
252	        '''

254	            raise NotImplementedError(
255	                "DXDataObject is an abstract class; a subclass should" + \
256	                    "be initialized instead.")
257	
258	        dx_hash, remaining_kwargs = self._get_creation_params(kwargs)
259	        self._new(dx_hash, **remaining_kwargs)
260	
261	    def set_id(self, dxid):
262	        '''
263	        :param dxid: Object ID or a DNAnexus link (a dict with key "$dnanexus_link"); if a project ID is provided in the DNAnexus link, it will also be used to set the project ID
264	        :type dxid: string or dict

266	        Equivalent to calling
267	        :meth:`~dxpy.bindings.DXDataObject.set_ids` with the same
268	        arguments.

271	
272	    def set_ids(self, dxid, project=None):
273	        '''
274	        :param dxid: Object ID or a DNAnexus link (a dict with key "$dnanexus_link"); if a project ID is provided in the DNAnexus link, it will be used as *project* unless *project* has been explictly provided
275	        :type dxid: string or dict
276	        :param project: Project ID
277	        :type project: string
278	
279	        Discards the currently stored ID and associates the handler with
280	        *dxid*. Associates the handler with the copy of the object in
281	        *project* (if no project is explicitly specified, the default
282	        data container is used).
283	
284	        '''
285	
286	        if is_dxlink(dxid):
287	            dxid, project_from_link = get_dxlink_ids(dxid)
288	            if project is None:
289	                project = project_from_link
290	
291	        if dxid is not None:
292	            verify_string_dxid(dxid, self._class)
293	        self._dxid = dxid
294	
295	        if project is None:
296	            self._proj = dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID
297	        elif project is not None:

299	            self._proj = project
300	
301	    def get_proj_id(self):
302	        '''
303	        :returns: Project ID of associated object
304	        :rtype: string
305	
306	        Returns the project ID, if any, that the handler is currently
307	        associated with.
308	
309	        '''

311	        return self._proj
312	
313	    def describe(self, incl_properties=False, incl_details=False, fields=None, default_fields=None, **kwargs):
314	        """
315	        :param fields: set of fields to include in the output, for
316	            example ``{'name', 'modified'}``. The field ``id`` is always
317	            implicitly included. If ``fields`` is specified, the default
318	            fields are not included (that is, only the fields specified
319	            here, and ``id``, are included) unless ``default_fields`` is
320	            additionally set to True.
321	        :type fields: set or sequence of str
322	        :param default_fields: if True, include the default fields in
323	            addition to fields requested in ``fields``, if any; if
324	            False, only the fields specified in ``fields``, if any, are
325	            returned (defaults to False if ``fields`` is specified, True
326	            otherwise)
327	        :type default_fields: bool
328	        :param incl_properties: if true, includes the properties of the
329	            object in the output (deprecated; use
330	            ``fields={'properties'}, default_fields=True`` instead)
331	        :type incl_properties: bool
332	        :param incl_details: if true, includes the details of the object
333	            in the output (deprecated; use ``fields={'details'},
334	            default_fields=True`` instead)
335	        :type incl_details: bool
336	        :returns: Description of the remote object
337	        :rtype: dict
338	
339	        Return a dict with a description of the remote data object.
340	
341	        The result includes the key-value pairs as specified in the API
342	        documentation for the ``/describe`` method of each data object
343	        class. The API defines some default set of fields that will be
344	        included (at a minimum, "id", "class", etc. should be available,
345	        and there may be additional fields that vary based on the
346	        class); the set of fields may be customized using ``fields`` and
347	        ``default_fields``.
348	
349	        Any project-specific metadata fields (name, properties, and
350	        tags) are obtained from the copy of the object in the project
351	        associated with the handler, if possible.
352	
353	        """
354	
355	        if self._dxid is None:
356	            raise DXError('This {handler} handler has not been initialized with a {_class} ID and cannot be described'.format(
357	                handler=self.__class__.__name__,
358	                _class=self._class)
359	            )
360	
361	        if (incl_properties or incl_details) and (fields is not None or default_fields is not None):
362	            raise ValueError('Cannot specify properties or details in conjunction with fields or default_fields')
363	
364	        if incl_properties or incl_details:
365	            describe_input = dict(properties=incl_properties, details=incl_details)
366	        else:
367	            describe_input = {}
368	            if default_fields is not None:
369	                describe_input['defaultFields'] = default_fields
370	            if fields is not None:
371	                describe_input['fields'] = {field_name: True for field_name in fields}
372	
373	        if self._proj is not None:
374	            describe_input["project"] = self._proj
375	
376	        self._desc = self._describe(self._dxid, describe_input, **kwargs)
377	
378	        return self._desc
379	
380	    def add_types(self, types, **kwargs):
381	        """
382	        :param types: Types to add to the object
383	        :type types: list of strings
384	        :raises: :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError` if the object is not in the "open" state
385	
386	        Adds each of the specified types to the remote object. Takes no
387	        action for types that are already listed for the object.
388	
389	        """
390	
391	        self._add_types(self._dxid, {"types": types}, **kwargs)
392	
393	    def remove_types(self, types, **kwargs):
394	        """
395	        :param types: Types to remove from the object
396	        :type types: list of strings
397	        :raises: :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError` if the object is not in the "open" state
398	
399	        Removes each the specified types from the remote object. Takes
400	        no action for types that the object does not currently have.
401	
402	        """
403	
404	        self._remove_types(self._dxid, {"types": types}, **kwargs)
405	
406	    def get_details(self, **kwargs):
407	        """
408	        Returns the contents of the details of the object.
409	
410	        :rtype: list or dict
411	        """
412	
413	        return self._get_details(self._dxid, **kwargs)
414	
415	    def set_details(self, details, **kwargs):
416	        """
417	        :param details: Details to set for the object
418	        :type details: dict or list
419	        :raises: :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError` if the object is not in the "open" state
420	
421	        Sets the details for the remote object with the specified value.
422	        If the input contains the string ``"$dnanexus_link"`` as a key
423	        in a hash, it must be the only key in the hash, and its value
424	        must be a valid ID of an existing object.
425	
426	        """
427	
428	        return self._set_details(self._dxid, details, **kwargs)
429	
430	    def hide(self, **kwargs):
431	        """
432	        :raises: :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError` if the object is not in the "open" state
433	
434	        Hides the remote object.
435	
436	        """
437	
438	        return self._set_visibility(self._dxid, {"hidden": True}, **kwargs)
439	
440	    def unhide(self, **kwargs):
441	        """
442	        :raises: :class:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError` if the object is not in the "open" state
443	
444	        Makes the remote object visible.
445	
446	        """
447	
448	        return self._set_visibility(self._dxid, {"hidden": False}, **kwargs)
449	
450	    def rename(self, name, **kwargs):
451	        """
452	        :param name: New name for the object
453	        :type name: string
454	
455	        Renames the remote object.
456	
457	        The name is changed on the copy of the object in the project
458	        associated with the handler.
459	
460	        """
461	
462	        return self._rename(self._dxid, {"project": self._proj,
463	                                         "name": name}, **kwargs)
464	
465	    def get_properties(self, **kwargs):
466	        """
467	        :returns: Properties given as key-value pairs of strings
468	        :rtype: dict
469	
470	        Returns the properties of the object.
471	
472	        The properties are read from the copy of the object in the
473	        project associated with the handler.
474	
475	        """
476	        return self.describe(incl_properties=True, **kwargs)["properties"]
477	
478	    def set_properties(self, properties, **kwargs):
479	        """
480	        :param properties: Property names and values given as key-value pairs of strings
481	        :type properties: dict
482	
483	        Given key-value pairs in *properties* for property names and
484	        values, the properties are set on the object for the given
485	        property names. Any property with a value of :const:`None`
486	        indicates the property will be deleted.

32	def resolve_data_objects(objects, project=None, folder=None, batchsize=1000):
33	    """
34	    :param objects: Data object specifications, each with fields "name"
35	                    (required), "folder", and "project"
36	    :type objects: list of dictionaries
37	    :param project: ID of project context; a data object's project defaults
38	                    to this if not specified for that object
39	    :type project: string
40	    :param folder: Folder path within the project; a data object's folder
41	                   path defaults to this if not specified for that object
42	    :type folder: string
43	    :param batchsize: Number of objects to resolve in each batch call to
44	                      system_resolve_data_objects; defaults to 1000 and is
45	                      only used for testing (must be a positive integer not
46	                      exceeding 1000)
47	    :type batchsize: int
48	    :returns: List of results parallel to input objects, where each
49	              entry is a list containing 0 or more dicts, each corresponding
50	              to a resolved object
51	    :rtype: List of lists of dictionaries
52	
53	    Each returned element is a list of dictionaries with keys "project" and
54	    "id". The number of dictionaries for each element may be 0, 1, or more.
55	    """
56	    if not isinstance(batchsize, int) or batchsize <= 0 or batchsize > 1000:
57	        raise ValueError("batchsize for resolve_data_objects must be a positive integer not exceeding 1000")
58	    args = {}
59	    if project:
60	        args.update({'project': project})
61	    if folder:
62	        args.update({'folder': folder})
63	
64	    results = []
65	
66	    # Call API method /system/resolveDataObjects in groups of size batchsize
67	    for i in range(0, len(objects), batchsize):
68	        args.update({'objects': objects[i:(i+batchsize)]})
69	        results.extend(dxpy.api.system_resolve_data_objects(args)['results'])
70	    return results

73	def _find(api_method, query, limit, return_handler, first_page_size, **kwargs):
74	    ''' Takes an API method handler (dxpy.api.find*) and calls it with *query*,
75	    and then wraps a generator around its output. Used by the methods below.
76	
77	    Note that this function may only be used for /system/find* methods.
78	    '''
79	    num_results = 0
80	
81	    if "limit" not in query:
82	        query["limit"] = first_page_size
83	
84	    while True:
85	        resp = api_method(query, **kwargs)
86	
87	        by_parent = resp.get('byParent')
88	        descriptions = resp.get('describe')
89	        def format_result(result):
90	            if return_handler:
91	                result = dxpy.get_handler(result['id'], project=result.get('project'))
92	            if by_parent is not None:
93	                return result, by_parent, descriptions
94	            else:
95	                return result
96	
97	        for i in resp["results"]:
98	            if num_results == limit:
99	                return
100	            num_results += 1
101	            yield format_result(i)
102	
103	        # set up next query
104	        if resp["next"] is not None:
105	            query["starting"] = resp["next"]
106	            query["limit"] = min(query["limit"]*2, 1000)
107	        else:
108	            return

112	                      typename=None, tag=None, tags=None,
113	                      link=None, project=None, folder=None, recurse=None,
114	                      modified_after=None, modified_before=None,
115	                      created_after=None, created_before=None,
116	                      describe=False, limit=None, level=None, region=None,
117	                      archival_state=None, return_handler=False, first_page_size=100,
118	                      **kwargs):
119	    """
120	    :param classname:
121	        Class with which to restrict the search, i.e. one of "record",
122	        "file", "applet", "workflow", "database"
123	    :type classname: string

131	    :type name_mode: string

133	    :type properties: dict

137	    :type tag: string

139	    :type tags: list of strings

141	    :type link: string
142	    :param project: ID of a project in which each result must appear
143	    :type project: string

145	    :type folder: string

147	    :type recurse: boolean
148	    :param modified_after: Timestamp after which each result was last modified (see note below for interpretation)
149	    :type modified_after: int or string
150	    :param modified_before: Timestamp before which each result was last modified (see note below for interpretation)
151	    :type modified_before: int or string
152	    :param created_after: Timestamp after which each result was last created (see note below for interpretation)
153	    :type created_after: int or string
154	    :param created_before: Timestamp before which each result was last created (see note below for interpretation)
155	    :type created_before: int or string
156	    :param describe: Controls whether to also return the output of
157	        calling describe() on each object. Supply False to omit describe
158	        output, True to obtain the default describe output, or a dict to
159	        be supplied as the describe call input (which may, among other
160	        things, be used to customize the set of fields that is returned)
161	    :type describe: bool or dict
162	    :param level: The minimum permissions level for which results should be returned (one of "VIEW", "UPLOAD", "CONTRIBUTE", or "ADMINISTER")
163	    :type level: string

166	    :param archival_state: Filter by the given archival state (one of "archived", "live", "archival", "unarchiving", or "any"). Requires classname="file", project, and folder arguments to be provided.
167	    :type archival_state: string 
168	    :param limit: The maximum number of results to be returned (if not specified, the number of results is unlimited)
169	    :type limit: int
170	    :param first_page_size: The number of results that the initial API call will return. Subsequent calls will raise this by multiplying by 2 up to a maximum of 1000.
171	    :type first_page_size: int
172	    :param return_handler: If True, yields results as dxpy object handlers (otherwise, yields each result as a dict with keys "id" and "project")
173	    :type return_handler: boolean
174	    :rtype: generator
175	
176	    Returns a generator that yields all data objects matching the query,
177	    up to *limit* objects. It transparently handles paging through the
178	    result set if necessary. For all parameters that are omitted, the
179	    search is not restricted by the corresponding field.
180	
181	    .. note:: All timestamps must be supplied as one of the following:
182	
183	       * A nonnegative integer, interpreted as milliseconds since the Epoch
184	       * A negative integer, interpreted as an offset in milliseconds relative

1928	    A class to handle record objects of type Dataset.
1929	    Inherits from DXRecord, but automatically populates default fields, details and properties.
1930	
1931	    Attributes:
1932	        All the same as DXRecord

1934	        description - from record details
1935	        schema - from record details
1936	        version - from record details
1937	        descriptor - DXDatasetDescriptor object
1938	    Functions
1939	        get_descriptor - calls DXDatasetDescriptor(descriptor_dxfile) if descriptor is None
1940	        get_dictionary - calls descriptor.get_dictionary
1941	
1942	    """

1944	    _record_type = "Dataset"
1945	
1946	    def __init__(self, dxid=None, project=None):
1947	        super(DXDataset, self).__init__(dxid, project)
1948	        self.describe(default_fields=True, fields={"properties", "details"})
1949	        assert self._record_type in self.types
1950	        assert "descriptor" in self.details
1951	        if is_dxlink(self.details["descriptor"]):
1952	            self.descriptor_dxfile = DXFile(self.details["descriptor"], mode="rb", project=project)

65	        if fields is not None:
66	            describe_input['fields'] = fields
67	        self._desc = dxpy.api.analysis_describe(self._dxid, describe_input, **kwargs)
68	        return self._desc
69	
70	    def add_tags(self, tags, **kwargs):
71	        """
72	        :param tags: Tags to add to the analysis
73	        :type tags: list of strings
74	
75	        Adds each of the specified tags to the analysis. Takes no
76	        action for tags that are already listed for the analysis.
77	
78	        """
79	
80	        dxpy.api.analysis_add_tags(self._dxid, {"tags": tags}, **kwargs)
81	
82	    def remove_tags(self, tags, **kwargs):
83	        """
84	        :param tags: Tags to remove from the analysis
85	        :type tags: list of strings
86	
87	        Removes each of the specified tags from the analysis. Takes
88	        no action for tags that the analysis does not currently have.
89	
90	        """
91	
92	        dxpy.api.analysis_remove_tags(self._dxid, {"tags": tags}, **kwargs)
93	
94	    def set_properties(self, properties, **kwargs):
95	        """
96	        :param properties: Property names and values given as key-value pairs of strings
97	        :type properties: dict
98	
99	        Given key-value pairs in *properties* for property names and
100	        values, the properties are set on the analysis for the given
101	        property names. Any property with a value of :const:`None`
102	        indicates the property will be deleted.
103	
104	        .. note:: Any existing properties not mentioned in *properties*
105	           are not modified by this method.
106	
107	        """
108	
109	        dxpy.api.analysis_set_properties(self._dxid, {"properties": properties}, **kwargs)
110	
111	    def wait_on_done(self, interval=2, timeout=3600*24*7, **kwargs):
112	        '''
113	        :param interval: Number of seconds between queries to the analysis's state
114	        :type interval: integer
115	        :param timeout: Maximum amount of time to wait, in seconds, until the analysis is done (or at least partially failed)
116	        :type timeout: integer
117	        :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if the timeout is reached before the analysis has finished running, or :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXJobFailureError` if some job in the analysis has failed
118	
119	        Waits until the analysis has finished running.
120	        '''
121	
122	        elapsed = 0
123	        while True:
124	            state = self._get_state(**kwargs)
125	            if state == "done":
126	                break
127	            if state in ["failed", "partially_failed"]:
128	                desc = self.describe(**kwargs)
129	                err_msg = "Analysis has failed because of {failureReason}: {failureMessage}".format(**desc)
130	                if desc.get("failureFrom") != None and desc["failureFrom"]["id"] != desc["id"]:
131	                    err_msg += " (failure from {id})".format(id=desc['failureFrom']['id'])
132	                raise DXJobFailureError(err_msg)
133	            if state == "terminated":
134	                raise DXJobFailureError("Analysis was terminated.")
135	
136	            if elapsed >= timeout or elapsed < 0:
137	                raise DXJobFailureError("Reached timeout while waiting for the analysis to finish")
138	
139	            time.sleep(interval)
140	            elapsed += interval
141	
142	    def terminate(self, **kwargs):
143	        '''
144	        Terminates the associated analysis.
145	        '''
146	        dxpy.api.analysis_terminate(self._dxid, **kwargs)
147	
148	    def get_output_ref(self, field, index=None, metadata=None):
149	        '''
150	        :param field: Output field name of this analysis
151	        :type field: string
152	        :param index: If the referenced field is an array, optionally specify an index (starting from 0) to indicate a particular member of the array
153	        :type index: int
154	        :param metadata: If the referenced field is of a data object class, a string indicating the metadata that should be read, e.g. "name", "properties.propkey", "details.refgenome"
155	        :type metadata: string
156	
157	        Returns a dict containing a valid reference to an output of this analysis.
158	        '''
159	
160	        link = {"$dnanexus_link": {"analysis": self._dxid, "field": field}}
161	        if index is not None:
162	            link["$dnanexus_link"]["index"] = index
163	        if metadata is not None:
164	            link["$dnanexus_link"]["metadata"] = metadata
165	        return link
166	
167	    def _get_state(self, **kwargs):
168	        '''
169	        :returns: State of the remote object
170	        :rtype: string
171	
172	        Queries the API server for the analysis's state.
173	
174	        Note that this function is shorthand for:
175	
176	            dxanalysis.describe(**kwargs)["state"]
177	
178	        '''
179	
180	        return self.describe(fields=dict(state=True), **kwargs)["state"]

17	'''
18	Accessing App-Specific Containers
19	+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
20	
21	Apps have associated resource containers and project cache containers.
22	To easily access these, the following utility functions are provided.
23	These functions are meant to be called only by a job.
24	'''
25	
26	from __future__ import print_function, unicode_literals, division, absolute_import
27	
28	import os
29	
30	import dxpy
31	from ..exceptions import DXError
32	from .search import find_one_data_object
33	
34	def load_app_resource(**kwargs):
35	    '''
36	    :param kwargs: keyword args for :func:`~dxpy.bindings.search.find_one_data_object`, with the exception of "project"
37	    :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if "project" is given, if this is called with dxpy.JOB_ID not set, or if "DX_RESOURCES_ID" or "DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID" is not found in the environment variables
38	    :returns: None if no matching object is found; otherwise returns a dxpy object handler for that class of object
39	
40	    Searches for a data object in the app resources container matching the given keyword arguments.  If found, the
41	    object will be cloned into the running job's workspace container, and the handler for it will be returned. If the
42	    app resources container ID is not found in DX_RESOURCES_ID, falls back to looking in the current project.
43	
44	    Example::
45	
46	        @dxpy.entry_point('main')
47	        def main(*args, **kwargs):
48	            x = load_app_resource(name="Indexed genome", classname='file')
49	            dxpy.download_dxfile(x)
50	    '''
51	
52	    if 'project' in kwargs:
53	        raise DXError('Unexpected kwarg: "project"')
54	    if dxpy.JOB_ID is None:
55	        raise DXError('Not called by a job')
56	    if 'DX_RESOURCES_ID' not in os.environ and 'DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID' not in os.environ:
57	        raise DXError('App resources container ID could not be found')
58	
59	    kwargs['project'] = os.environ.get('DX_RESOURCES_ID', os.environ.get('DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID'))
60	    kwargs['return_handler'] = True
61	
62	    return find_one_data_object(**kwargs)
63	
64	def load_from_cache(**kwargs):
65	    '''
66	    :param kwargs: keyword args for :func:`~dxpy.bindings.search.find_one_data_object`, with the exception of "project"
67	    :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if "project" is given, if this is called with dxpy.JOB_ID not set, or if "DX_PROJECT_CACHE_ID" is not found in the environment variables
68	    :returns: None if no matching object is found; otherwise returns a dxpy object handler for that class of object
69	
70	    Searches for a data object in the project cache container matching
71	    the given keyword arguments.  If found, the object will be cloned
72	    into the running job's workspace container, and the handler for it
73	    will be returned.
74	
75	    Example::
76	
77	        @dxpy.entry_point('main')
78	        def main(*args, **kwargs):
79	            x = load_from_cache(name="Indexed genome", classname='file')
80	            if x is None:
81	                x = compute_result(*args)
82	                save_to_cache(x)
83	    '''
84	
85	    if 'project' in kwargs:
86	        raise DXError('Unexpected kwarg: "project"')
87	    if dxpy.JOB_ID is None:
88	        raise DXError('Not called by a job')
89	    if 'DX_PROJECT_CACHE_ID' not in os.environ:
90	        raise DXError('Project cache ID could not be found in the environment variable DX_PROJECT_CACHE_ID')
91	
92	    kwargs['project'] = os.environ.get('DX_PROJECT_CACHE_ID')
93	    kwargs['return_handler'] = True
94	
95	    cached_object = find_one_data_object(**kwargs)
96	
97	    if cached_object is None:
98	        return None
99	
100	    return cached_object.clone(dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID)
101	
102	# Maybe this should be a member function of a data object?
103	def save_to_cache(dxobject):
104	    '''
105	    :param dxobject: a dxpy object handler for an object to save to the cache
106	    :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.DXError` if this is called with dxpy.JOB_ID not set, or if "DX_PROJECT_CACHE_ID" is not found in the environment variables
107	
108	    Clones the given object to the project cache.
109	
110	    Example::
111	
112	        @dxpy.entry_point('main')
113	        def main(*args, **kwargs):
114	            x = load_from_cache(name="Indexed genome", classname='file')
115	            if x is None:
116	                x = compute_result(*args)
117	                save_to_cache(x)
118	    '''
119	
120	    if dxpy.JOB_ID is None:
121	        raise DXError('Not called by a job')
122	    if 'DX_PROJECT_CACHE_ID' not in os.environ:
123	        raise DXError('Project cache ID could not be found in the environment variable DX_PROJECT_CACHE_ID')
124	
125	    dxobject.clone(os.environ.get('DX_PROJECT_CACHE_ID'))
126

17	'''
18	This submodule handles copy commands for the dx
19	command-line client.
20	
21	'dx cp' works only between DIFFERENT projects. It will exit fatally otherwise.
22	'''
23	
24	from __future__ import print_function, unicode_literals, division, absolute_import
25	
26	import dxpy
27	from ..utils.resolver import (resolve_existing_path, resolve_path, is_hashid, get_last_pos_of_char)
28	from ..exceptions import (err_exit, DXCLIError, ResourceNotFound)
29	from . import try_call
30	from dxpy.utils.printing import (fill)
31	
32	
33	def cp_to_noexistent_destination(args, dest_path, dx_dest, dest_proj):
34	    ''' Copy the source to a destination that does not currently
35	    exist. This involves creating the target file/folder.
36	    '''
37	    # Destination folder path is new => renaming
38	    if len(args.sources) != 1:
39	        # Can't copy and rename more than one object
40	        raise DXCLIError('The destination folder does not exist')
41	    last_slash_pos = get_last_pos_of_char('/', dest_path)
42	    if last_slash_pos == 0:
43	        dest_folder = '/'
44	    else:
45	        dest_folder = dest_path[:last_slash_pos]
46	    dest_name = dest_path[last_slash_pos + 1:].replace('\/', '/')
47	    try:
48	        dx_dest.list_folder(folder=dest_folder, only='folders')
49	    except dxpy.DXAPIError as e:
50	        if isinstance(e, ResourceNotFound):
51	            raise DXCLIError('The destination folder does not exist')
52	        else:
53	            raise
54	    except:
55	        err_exit()
56	
57	    # Clone and rename either the data object or the folder.
58	    # src_result is None if it could not be resolved to an object.
59	    src_proj, src_path, src_results = try_call(resolve_existing_path,
60	                                               args.sources[0],
61	                                               allow_mult=True, all_mult=args.all)
62	
63	    if src_proj == dest_proj:
64	        if is_hashid(args.sources[0]):
65	            # This is the only case in which the source project is
66	            # purely assumed, so give a better error message.
67	            raise DXCLIError(fill('Error: You must specify a source project for ' + args.sources[0]))
68	        else:
69	            raise DXCLIError(fill('A source path and the destination path resolved to the ' +
70	                                'same project or container.  Please specify different source ' +
71	                                'and destination containers, e.g.') +
72	                             '\n  dx cp source-project:source-id-or-path dest-project:dest-path')
73	
74	    if src_results is None:
75	        try:
76	            contents = dxpy.api.project_list_folder(src_proj,
77	                                                    {"folder": src_path, "includeHidden": True})
78	            dxpy.api.project_new_folder(dest_proj, {"folder": dest_path})
79	            exists = dxpy.api.project_clone(src_proj,
80	                                            {"folders": contents['folders'],
81	                                             "objects": [result['id'] for result in contents['objects']],
82	                                             "project": dest_proj,
83	                                             "destination": dest_path})['exists']
84	            if len(exists) > 0:
85	                print(fill('The following objects already existed in the destination ' +
86	                           'container and were not copied:') + '\n ' + '\n '.join(exists))
87	                return
88	        except:
89	            err_exit()
90	    else:
91	        try:
92	            exists = dxpy.api.project_clone(src_proj,
93	                                            {"objects": [result['id'] for result in src_results],
94	                                             "project": dest_proj,
95	                                             "destination": dest_folder})['exists']
96	            if len(exists) > 0:
97	                print(fill('The following objects already existed in the destination ' +
98	                           'container and were not copied:') + '\n ' + '\n '.join(exists))
99	            for result in src_results:
100	                if result['id'] not in exists:
101	                    dxpy.DXHTTPRequest('/' + result['id'] + '/rename',
102	                                       {"project": dest_proj,
103	                                        "name": dest_name})
104	            return
105	        except:
106	            err_exit()
107	
108	
109	def cp(args):
110	    dest_proj, dest_path, _none = try_call(resolve_path, args.destination, expected='folder')
111	    if dest_path is None:
112	        raise DXCLIError('Cannot copy to a hash ID')
113	    dx_dest = dxpy.get_handler(dest_proj)
114	    try:
115	        # check if the destination exists
116	        dx_dest.list_folder(folder=dest_path, only='folders')
117	    except:
118	        cp_to_noexistent_destination(args, dest_path, dx_dest, dest_proj)
119	        return
120	
121	    # The destination exists, we need to copy all of the sources to it.
122	    if len(args.sources) == 0:
123	        raise DXCLIError('No sources provided to copy to another project')
124	    src_objects = []
125	    src_folders = []
126	    for source in args.sources:
127	        src_proj, src_folderpath, src_results = try_call(resolve_existing_path,
128	                                                         source,
129	                                                         allow_mult=True, all_mult=args.all)
130	        if src_proj == dest_proj:
131	            if is_hashid(source):
132	                # This is the only case in which the source project is
133	                # purely assumed, so give a better error message.
134	                raise DXCLIError(fill('Error: You must specify a source project for ' + source))
135	            else:
136	                raise DXCLIError(fill('Error: A source path and the destination path resolved ' +
137	                                    'to the same project or container. Please specify ' +
138	                                    'different source and destination containers, e.g.') +
139	                                 '\n  dx cp source-project:source-id-or-path dest-project:dest-path')
140	
141	        if src_proj is None:
142	            raise DXCLIError(fill('Error: A source project must be specified or a current ' +
143	                                  'project set in order to clone objects between projects'))
144	
145	        if src_results is None:
146	            src_folders.append(src_folderpath)
147	        else:
148	            src_objects += [result['id'] for result in src_results]
149	    try:
150	        exists = dxpy.DXHTTPRequest('/' + src_proj + '/clone',
151	                                    {"objects": src_objects,
152	                                     "folders": src_folders,
153	                                     "project": dest_proj,
154	                                     "destination": dest_path,
155	                                     "targetFileRelocation": args.target_file_relocation})['exists']
156	        if len(exists) > 0:
157	            print(fill('The following objects already existed in the destination container ' +
158	                       'and were left alone:') + '\n ' + '\n '.join(exists))
159	    except:
160	        err_exit()

17	'''
18	DXDatabase Handler
19	**************
20	
21	This remote database handler is a Python database-like object.
22	'''
23	
24	from __future__ import print_function, unicode_literals, division, absolute_import
25	
26	import os, copy, time
27	from io import BytesIO
28	from threading import Lock
29	from multiprocessing import cpu_count
30	
31	import dxpy
32	from . import DXDataObject
33	from ..utils.resolver import object_exists_in_project
34	from .. import logger
35	from ..compat import basestring
36	
37	
38	DXFILE_HTTP_THREADS = min(cpu_count(), 8)
39	MIN_BUFFER_SIZE = 1024*1024
40	DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE = 1024*1024*16
41	if dxpy.JOB_ID:
42	    # Increase HTTP request buffer size when we are running within the
43	    # platform.
44	    DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE = 1024*1024*96
45	
46	MD5_READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 1024*1024*4
47	FILE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 60
48	
49	
50	def _validate_headers(headers):
51	    for key, value in headers.items():
52	        if not isinstance(key, basestring):
53	            raise ValueError("Expected key %r of headers to be a string" % (key,))
54	        if not isinstance(value, basestring):
55	            raise ValueError("Expected value %r of headers (associated with key %r) to be a string"
56	                             % (value, key))
57	    return headers
58	
59	
60	def _readable_part_size(num_bytes):
61	    "Returns the file size in readable form."
62	    B = num_bytes
63	    KB = float(1024)
64	    MB = float(KB * 1024)
65	    GB = float(MB * 1024)
66	    TB = float(GB * 1024)
67	
68	    if B < KB:
69	        return '{0} {1}'.format(B, 'bytes' if B != 1 else 'byte')
70	    elif KB <= B < MB:
71	        return '{0:.2f} KiB'.format(B/KB)
72	    elif MB <= B < GB:
73	        return '{0:.2f} MiB'.format(B/MB)
74	    elif GB <= B < TB:
75	        return '{0:.2f} GiB'.format(B/GB)
76	    elif TB <= B:
77	        return '{0:.2f} TiB'.format(B/TB)
78	
79	def do_debug(msg):
80	    logger.debug(msg)
81	
82	class DXDatabase(DXDataObject):
83	    '''Remote database object handler.
84	
85	    :param dxid: Object ID
86	    :type dxid: string
87	    :param project: Project ID
88	    :type project: string
89	
90	    '''
91	
92	    _class = "database"
93	
94	    _describe = staticmethod(dxpy.api.file_describe)
95	
96	    _http_threadpool_size = DXFILE_HTTP_THREADS
97	    _http_threadpool = dxpy.utils.get_futures_threadpool(max_workers=_http_threadpool_size)
98	
99	    NO_PROJECT_HINT = 'NO_PROJECT_HINT'
100	
101	    def __init__(self, dxid=None, project=None, read_buffer_size=DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE,
102	                 expected_file_size=None, file_is_mmapd=False):
103	        """
104	        :param dxid: Object ID
105	        :type dxid: string
106	        :param project: Project ID
107	        :type project: string
108	        :param read_buffer_size: size of read buffer in bytes
109	        :type read_buffer_size: int
110	        :param expected_file_size: size of data that will be written, if
111	            known
112	        :type expected_file_size: int
113	        :param file_is_mmapd: True if input file is mmap'd (if so, the
114	            write buffer size will be constrained to be a multiple of
115	            the allocation granularity)
116	        :type file_is_mmapd: bool
117	        """
118	
119	        DXDataObject.__init__(self, dxid=dxid, project=project)
120	
121	        self._read_buf = BytesIO()
122	        self._read_bufsize = read_buffer_size
123	        self._expected_file_size = expected_file_size
124	        self._file_is_mmapd = file_is_mmapd
125	
126	        # These are cached once for all download threads. This saves calls to the apiserver.
127	        self._download_url, self._download_url_headers, self._download_url_expires = None, None, None
128	
129	        # This lock protects accesses to the above three variables, ensuring that they would
130	        # be checked and changed atomically. This protects against thread race conditions.
131	        self._url_download_mutex = Lock()
132	
133	        self._request_iterator, self._response_iterator = None, None
134	        self._http_threadpool_futures = set()
135	
136	
137	    def get_download_url(self, filename=None, src_filename=None, project=None, **kwargs):
138	        """
139	        :param filename: desired filename of the local downloaded file
140	        :type filename: str
141	        :param project: ID of a project containing the file (the download URL
142	            will be associated with this project, and this may affect which
143	            billing account is billed for this download).
144	            If no project is specified, an attempt will be made to verify if the database is
145	            in the project from the DXDatabase handler (as specified by the user or
146	            the current project stored in dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID). Otherwise, no hint is supplied.
147	            This fall back behavior does not happen inside a job environment.
148	        :type project: str
149	        :returns: download URL and dict containing HTTP headers to be supplied
150	            with the request
151	        :rtype: tuple (str, dict)
152	        :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.ResourceNotFound` if a project context was
153	            given and the database was not found in that project context.
154	        :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.ResourceNotFound` if no project context was
155	            given and the database was not found in any projects.
156	
157	        Obtains a URL that can be used to directly download files associated
158	        with the specified database.
159	
160	        """
161	
162	        args = {}
163	
164	        if src_filename is not None:
165	            args["filename"] = src_filename
166	
167	        # If project=None, we fall back to the project attached to this handler
168	        # (if any). If this is supplied, it's treated as a hint: if it's a
169	        # project in which this file exists, it's passed on to the
170	        # apiserver. Otherwise, NO hint is supplied. In principle supplying a
171	        # project in the handler that doesn't contain this file ought to be an
172	        # error, but it's this way for backwards compatibility. We don't know
173	        # who might be doing downloads and creating handlers without being
174	        # careful that the project encoded in the handler contains the file
175	        # being downloaded. They may now rely on such behavior.
176	        if project is None and 'DX_JOB_ID' not in os.environ:
177	            project_from_handler = self.get_proj_id()
178	            if project_from_handler and object_exists_in_project(self.get_id(), project_from_handler):
179	                project = project_from_handler
180	
181	        if project is not None and project is not DXDatabase.NO_PROJECT_HINT:
182	            args["projectContext"] = project
183	
184	        # Test hook to write 'project' argument passed to API call to a
185	        # local file
186	        if '_DX_DUMP_BILLED_PROJECT' in os.environ:
187	            with open(os.environ['_DX_DUMP_BILLED_PROJECT'], "w") as fd:
188	                if project is not None and project != DXDatabase.NO_PROJECT_HINT:
189	                    fd.write(project)
190	
191	        with self._url_download_mutex:
192	
193	            if self._download_url is None or self._download_url_expires < time.time():
194	                # The idea here is to cache a download URL for the entire file, that will
195	                # be good for a few minutes. This avoids each thread having to ask the
196	                # server for a URL, increasing server load.
197	                #
198	                # To avoid thread race conditions, this check/update procedure is protected
199	                # with a lock.
200	
201	                # logging.debug("Download URL unset or expired, requesting a new one")
202	                if "timeout" not in kwargs:
203	                    kwargs["timeout"] = FILE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
204	                do_debug("dxdatabase get_download_url - download_file args = {}".format(args))
205	                resp = dxpy.api.database_download_file(self._dxid, args, **kwargs)
206	                do_debug("dxdatabase get_download_url - download_file resp = {}".format(resp));
207	                self._download_url = resp["url"]
208	                self._download_url_headers = _validate_headers(resp.get("headers", {}))
209	                self._download_url_expires = 32503680000  # doesn't expire (year 3000)
210	
211	            # Make a copy, ensuring each thread has its own mutable
212	            # version of the headers.  Note: python strings are
213	            # immutable, so we can safely give a reference to the
214	            # download url.
215	            retval_download_url = self._download_url
216	            retval_download_url_headers = copy.copy(self._download_url_headers)
217	
218	        return retval_download_url, retval_download_url_headers

36	# Check if a program (wget, curl, etc.) is on the path, and
37	# can be called.
38	def _which(program):
39	    def is_exe(fpath):
40	        return os.path.isfile(fpath) and os.access(fpath, os.X_OK)
41	
42	    for path in os.environ["PATH"].split(os.pathsep):
43	        exe_file = os.path.join(path, program)
44	        if is_exe(exe_file):
45	            return exe_file
46	    return None

48	# Caluclate the md5 checkum for [filename], and raise
49	# an exception if the checksum is wrong.
50	def _verify(filename, md5digest):
51	    md5sum_exe = _which("md5sum")
52	    if md5sum_exe is None:
53	        err_exit("md5sum is not installed on this system")
54	    cmd = [md5sum_exe, "-b", filename]
55	    try:
56	        print("Calculating checksum")
57	        cmd_out = subprocess.check_output(cmd)
58	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
59	        err_exit("Failed to run md5sum: " + str(cmd))
60	
61	    line = cmd_out.strip().split()
62	    if len(line) != 2:
63	        err_exit("md5sum returned weird results: " + str(line))
64	    actual_md5 = line[0]
65	    if actual_md5 != md5digest:
66	        err_exit("Checksum doesn't match " + actual_md5 + "  expected:" + md5digest)
67	    print("Checksum correct")

70	def download_one_file(project, file_desc, dest_filename, args):
71	    if not args.overwrite:
72	        if os.path.exists(dest_filename):
73	            err_exit(fill('Error: path "' + dest_filename + '" already exists but -f/--overwrite was not set'))
74	
75	    if file_desc['class'] != 'file':
76	        print("Skipping non-file data object {name} ({id})".format(**file_desc), file=sys.stderr)
77	        return
78	
79	    if file_desc['state'] != 'closed':
80	        print("Skipping file {name} ({id}) because it is not closed".format(**file_desc), file=sys.stderr)
81	        return
82	
83	    try:
84	        show_progress = args.show_progress
85	    except AttributeError:
86	        show_progress = False
87	
88	
89	    try:
90	        symlink_max_tries = args.symlink_max_tries if vars(args).get('symlink_max_tries') is not None else 15
91	        dxpy.download_dxfile(
92	                            file_desc['id'],
93	                            dest_filename,
94	                            show_progress=show_progress,
95	                            project=project,
96	                            describe_output=file_desc,
97	                            symlink_max_tries=symlink_max_tries)
98	        return
99	    except:
100	        err_exit()

103	    logging.debug(msg)

105	# dest_filename = local file where downloaded file will go
106	# src_filename = name of parquet file or folder being downloaded from database
107	def download_one_database_file(project, database_desc, dest_filename, src_filename, file_status, args):
108	    do_debug("download.py#download_one_database_file - src_filename = {}".format(src_filename));
109	    if file_status is not None:
110	        do_debug("download.py#download_one_database_file - file_status = {}".format(file_status));
111	
112	    if not args.overwrite:
113	        if os.path.exists(dest_filename):
114	            err_exit(fill('Error: path "' + dest_filename + '" already exists but -f/--overwrite was not set'))
115	
116	    if database_desc['class'] != 'database':
117	        print("Skipping non-database data object {name} ({id})".format(**database_desc), file=sys.stderr)
118	        return

120	    try:

138	def _ensure_local_dir(d):
139	    if not os.path.isdir(d):
140	        if os.path.exists(d):
141	            err_exit(fill('Error: path "' + d + '" already exists and is not a directory'))
142	        os.makedirs(d)
143	
144	
145	def _is_glob(path):
146	    return get_first_pos_of_char('*', path) > -1 or get_first_pos_of_char('?', path) > -1
147	
148	
149	def _rel2abs(path, project):
150	    if path.startswith('/') or dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID != project:
151	        abs_path, strip_prefix = path, os.path.dirname(path.rstrip('/'))
152	    else:
153	        wd = dxpy.config.get('DX_CLI_WD', u'/')
154	        abs_path, strip_prefix = os.path.join(wd, path), os.path.dirname(os.path.join(wd, path).rstrip('/'))
155	    if len(abs_path) > 1:
156	        abs_path = abs_path.rstrip('/')
157	    return abs_path, strip_prefix
158	
159	
160	def _download_files(files, destdir, args, dest_filename=None):
161	    for project in files:
162	        for f in files[project]:
163	            file_desc = f['describe']
164	            dest = dest_filename or os.path.join(destdir, file_desc['name'].replace('/', '%2F'))
165	            download_one_file(project, file_desc, dest, args)
166	
167	
168	def _download_folders(folders, destdir, args):
169	    try:
170	        show_progress = args.show_progress
171	    except AttributeError:
172	        show_progress = False
173	    for project in folders:
174	        for folder, strip_prefix in folders[project]:
175	            if not args.recursive:
176	                err_exit('Error: "' + folder + '" is a folder but the -r/--recursive option was not given')
177	            assert(folder.startswith(strip_prefix))
178	            folder_destdir = os.path.join(destdir, folder[len(strip_prefix):].lstrip('/'))
179	            try:
180	                dxpy.download_folder(project, folder_destdir, folder=folder, overwrite=args.overwrite,
181	                                     show_progress=show_progress)
182	            except:
183	                err_exit()
184	
185	
186	# Main entry point.
187	def download(args):
188	    folders_to_get, files_to_get, count = collections.defaultdict(list), collections.defaultdict(list), 0
189	    foldernames, filenames = [], []
190	    for path in args.paths:
191	        # Attempt to resolve name. If --all is given or the path looks like a glob, download all matches.
192	        # Otherwise, the resolver will display a picker (or error out if there is no tty to display to).
193	        resolver_kwargs = {'allow_empty_string': False}
194	        if args.all or _is_glob(path):
195	            resolver_kwargs.update({'allow_mult': True, 'all_mult': True})
196	
197	        # include "parts" and a few additional fields in the description so that
198	        # we don't have to call a separate describe method downstream
199	        resolver_kwargs.update({"describe": {"parts": True,
200	                                             "size": True,
201	                                             "drive": True,
202	                                             "md5": True,
203	                                             "checksumType": True
204	                                             }})
205	
206	        project, folderpath, matching_files = try_call(resolve_existing_path, path, **resolver_kwargs)
207	
208	        if matching_files is None:
209	            matching_files = []
210	        elif not isinstance(matching_files, list):
211	            matching_files = [matching_files]
212	
213	        # TODO: this could also be returned as metadata by resolve_path since
214	        # resolve_path knows these things in some circumstances
215	        path_has_explicit_proj = is_project_explicit(path) or is_jbor_str(path)
216	
217	        if is_jbor_str(path):
218	            assert len(matching_files) == 1
219	            project = matching_files[0]["describe"]["project"]
220	        matching_folders = []
221	        # project may be none if path is an ID and there is no project context
222	        if project is not None:
223	            colon_pos = get_first_pos_of_char(":", path)
224	            if colon_pos >= 0:
225	                path = path[colon_pos + 1:]
226	            abs_path, strip_prefix = _rel2abs(path, project)
227	            parent_folder = os.path.dirname(abs_path)
228	            folder_listing = dxpy.list_subfolders(project, parent_folder, recurse=False)
229	            matching_folders = pathmatch.filter(folder_listing, abs_path)
230	            if '/' in matching_folders and len(matching_folders) > 1:
231	                # The list of subfolders is {'/', '/A', '/B'}.
232	                # Remove '/', otherwise we will download everything twice.
233	                matching_folders.remove('/')
234	
235	        if len(matching_files) == 0 and len(matching_folders) == 0:
236	            err_exit(fill('Error: {path} is neither a file nor a folder name'.format(path=path)))
237	
238	        # If the user did not explicitly provide the project, don't pass any
239	        # project parameter to the API call but continue with the download.
240	        if not path_has_explicit_proj:
241	            project = dxpy.DXFile.NO_PROJECT_HINT
242	
243	        # If the user explicitly provided the project and it doesn't contain
244	        # the files, don't allow the download.
245	
246	        # For speed's sake, skip this check (i.e. one API call) if the user
247	        # passed the lightweight argument
248	        #
249	        # If length of matching_files is 0 then we're only downloading folders
250	        # so skip this logic since the files will be verified in the API call.
251	        if not args.lightweight \
252	            and len(matching_files) > 0 \
253	            and path_has_explicit_proj \
254	            and not any(object_exists_in_project(f['describe']['id'], project) for f in matching_files):
255	                err_exit(fill('Error: specified project does not contain specified file object'))
256	
257	        files_to_get[project].extend(matching_files)
258	        folders_to_get[project].extend(((f, strip_prefix) for f in matching_folders))
259	        count += len(matching_files) + len(matching_folders)
260	        filenames.extend(f["describe"]["name"] for f in matching_files)
261	        foldernames.extend(f[len(strip_prefix):].lstrip('/') for f in matching_folders)
262	
263	    if len(filenames) > 0 and len(foldernames) > 0:
264	        name_conflicts = set(filenames) & set(foldernames)
265	        if len(name_conflicts) > 0:
266	            msg = "Error: The following paths are both file and folder names, and " \
267	                  "cannot be downloaded to the same destination: "
268	            msg += ", ".join(sorted(name_conflicts))
269	            err_exit(fill(msg))
270	
271	    if args.output is None:
272	        destdir, dest_filename = os.getcwd(), None
273	    elif count > 1:
274	        if not os.path.exists(args.output):
275	            err_exit(fill("Error: When downloading multiple objects, --output must be an existing directory"))
276	        destdir, dest_filename = args.output, None
277	    elif os.path.isdir(args.output):
278	        destdir, dest_filename = args.output, None
279	    elif args.output.endswith('/'):
280	        err_exit(fill("Error: {path} could not be found".format(path=args.output)))
281	    else:
282	        destdir, dest_filename = os.getcwd(), args.output
283	
284	    _download_folders(folders_to_get, destdir, args)
285	    _download_files(files_to_get, destdir, args, dest_filename=dest_filename)

710	        # TODO: detect this error more reliably

775	
776	    if src_dir:

786	
787	    if billTo:
788	        app_spec["billTo"] = billTo
789	    if not try_versions:
790	        try_versions = [app_spec["version"]]
791	
792	    for version in try_versions:
793	        logger.debug("Attempting to create version %s..." % (version,))
794	        app_spec['version'] = version
795	
796	        app_describe = None
797	        try:
798	            # 404, which is rather likely in this app_describe request
799	            # (the purpose of the request is to find out whether the
800	            # version of interest exists), would ordinarily cause this
801	            # request to be retried multiple times, introducing a
802	            # substantial delay. So we disable retrying here for this
803	            # request.
804	            app_describe = dxpy.api.app_describe("app-" + app_spec["name"], alias=version, always_retry=False)
805	        except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError as e:
806	            if e.name == 'ResourceNotFound':
807	                pass
808	            else:
809	                raise e
810	        # Now app_describe is None if the app didn't exist, OR it contains the
811	        # app describe content.
812	
813	        # The describe check does not eliminate race conditions since an app
814	        # may always have been created, or published, since we last looked at
815	        # it. So the describe that happens here is just to save time and avoid
816	        # unnecessary API calls, but we always have to be prepared to recover
817	        # from API errors.
818	        if app_describe is None:
819	            logger.debug('App %s/%s does not yet exist' % (app_spec["name"], version))
820	            app_id = _create_or_update_version(app_spec['name'], app_spec['version'], app_spec, try_update=try_update)
821	            if app_id is None:
822	                continue
823	            if not brief:
824	                logger.info("Created app " + app_id)
825	            # Success!
826	            break
827	        elif app_describe.get("published", 0) == 0:
828	            logger.debug('App %s/%s already exists and has not been published' % (app_spec["name"], version))
829	            app_id = _update_version(app_spec['name'], app_spec['version'], app_spec, try_update=try_update)
830	            if app_id is None:
831	                continue
832	            if not brief:
833	                logger.info("Updated existing app " + app_id)
834	            # Success!
835	            break
836	        else:
837	            logger.debug('App %s/%s already exists and has been published' % (app_spec["name"], version))
838	            # App has already been published. Give up on this version.
839	            continue
840	    else:
841	        # All versions requested failed
842	        if len(try_versions) != 1:
843	            tried_versions = 'any of the requested versions: ' + ', '.join(try_versions)
844	        else:
